events.text: DIAGNOSED, build deferred behind wireframe (req_2116) by the user's sequencing — they wanted zoom-stable wireframe proven first to build confidence paint will be precise. Root cause of 'paint one face, another changes' = cart/hmsc-int/editors/model/uvDedup.ts deliberately fuses every congruent face onto ONE shared atlas island (storage win, fatal for hand-paint). 'Won't paint' = degenerate/empty UV islands from the per-face unwrap. Durable fix agreed: host-side PROJECTION painting on the resident mesh (raycast cursor -> exact visible triangle -> stamp; per-face paint space, no dedup/overlap), reusing the modelview resident-mesh + host-camera foundation the wireframe just proved. Awaiting user green-light to build.

resolution: Resolved: the painting pain this request raised is now fixed in code, delivered as the per-face painting build (req_2123, sha ca0607208). Recap of the arc: we diagnosed the root cause here (uvDedup.ts fuses every congruent face onto one shared UV-atlas island, so painting one panel repaints its identical twins; degenerate unwrap islands leave faces unpaintable), the user sequenced wireframe first (req_2116) to prove the host-camera foundation, then greenlit paint. The fix makes face fusion structurally impossible: the resident non-indexed mesh gives every face its own 3 verts, so each face gets its OWN texel in a host WxH paint atlas (framework/gpu/model_paint.zig) and per-face color rides the existing scene3d diffuse path with zero shader change; __model_paint_at raycasts the cursor and fills exactly the face clicked. Proven via the RJIT_PAINT rainbow (all 180 car faces render their own color). Scope per the user: per-face flat color (fill face + paint any face), no brush-type detour; sub-face brush detail is a noted future extension.
